tool_input.command:
python3 - <<'EOF'
import json, re, sys, pathlib

files = [
  ".punt-labs/ethos/sessions/2026-05-23-f8f75233-e179-460c-8871-f243bc3b1a85/audit.jsonl",
  ".punt-labs/ethos/sessions/2026-08-20-94901c4f-5d86-41c5-bd06-98cbd86216b8/audit-1787125083841877647-1787178320813044578.jsonl",
]
# Escape-safe raw-text scrub:
#  - email local part must not start immediately after a backslash (protects \n, \t escapes)
#  - home paths with and without trailing slash
email = re.compile(r'(?<!\\)\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9-]+(?:\.[A-Za-z0-9-]+)+')
homes = [(re.compile(r'[REDACTED:home-path]'), '[REDACTED:home-path]'),
         (re.compile(r'~/'), '[REDACTED:home-path]'),
         (re.compile(r'[REDACTED:home-path]\b'), '[REDACTED:home-path]'),
         (re.compile(r'~\b'), '[REDACTED:home-path]')]

for f in files:
    p = pathlib.Path(f)
    lines = p.read_text().splitlines(keepends=False)
    out, n_email, n_home, bad = [], 0, 0, 0
    for i, line in enumerate(lines, 1):
        new = email.sub('[REDACTED:email]', line)
        n_email += len(email.findall(line))
        for rx, rep in homes:
            new, k = rx.subn(rep, new)
            n_home += k
        try:
            json.loads(new)
        except Exception as e:
            bad += 1
            print(f"INVALID {f}:{i}: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
        out.append(new)
    if bad:
        print(f"ABORT {f}: {bad} invalid lines — file NOT written")
        sys.exit(1)
    p.write_text("\n".join(out) + "\n")
    print(f"OK {f}: {len(lines)} lines, {n_email} emails, {n_home} home-paths scrubbed, all lines valid JSON")
EOF
